CLASS 32 · PRESCHOOL AGES 4–5

Life Skills & Good Habits

Age 4–5 YearsClass 32Activities 29 live of 30Subjects Hygiene · manners · independence

The everyday skills grown-ups use without thinking — washing hands, tidying up, kind words, asking for help — learned the way four-year-olds learn best: on real activity sheets, doing the circle, the match, the trace and the draw all by themselves.

Every activity opens right here on the site: the sheet sits on the left and your child writes, circles, traces and draws straight on top of it. The instructions sit beside them in grown-up read-aloud words. Their finished work saves as a real picture they can keep.

Start the first activity →One or two sheets per sitting is a full class.

FOR GROWN-UPS

Every sheet follows five friendly steps.

The sheets keep one shape on purpose: after the first sheet your child already knows how to play the next one. The same five moves, new good habits.

  1. 1

    Circle it

    One right picture to circle — looking closely is the whole game.

  2. 2

    Match them

    Draw lines from the left side to the right side.

  3. 3

    Choose one

    Two choices — tick or circle the one that fits.

  4. 4

    Trace it

    Big tracing words, any color you like.

  5. 5

    Draw it

    The last box is all yours — draw!

Nothing is scored and nothing is timed. A sheet your child saved is a sheet finished — the “Cleared!” ribbon is theirs to keep, saved separately for each child you set up in My Classroom.

A NOTE FROM THE PRINCIPAL

For the grown-ups.

Life skills are not learned from a poster — they are practised on real days, with real hands. These sheets give the practice a picture: your child circles the child washing hands, and somewhere that evening they will wash theirs with a little more purpose. Keep the words big, the praise specific and the sessions short. The drawing layer is a real pencil as far as a four-year-old is concerned, and saving their finished sheet — their own circles and squiggles over the real artwork — is the proudest ending there is.
